notes: BATCH_002 Banking and Financial Awareness part: 200 original questions (60 Basic, 80 Intermediate, 60 Advanced) across 32 topics, IDs BANK_BFA_000204 to BANK_BFA_000403. Includes the time-sensitive topics Repo Rate (MPC decisions of December 2025, August 2026 and October 2026) and Budget and Economic Survey (Union Budget 2026-27 of 1 February 2026; Economic Survey 2025-26 of 29 January 2026). Every question carries fact checks against primary sources (RBI, PIB, DFS, SEBI, AMFI, BIS, IBBI, BSE) opened on 2026-11-05, or search-confirmed where the official page could not be fetched (marked web:search-confirmed). Changeable values carry current_affairs dates. Computed answers are re-derived in tools/batch_002/banking.py. Facts tested in BATCH_000/BATCH_001 are not repeated.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: As per RBI, a savings or current account is treated as 'inoperative' when there have been no customer-induced transactions in it for a period of over:

solution.explanation: RBI treats a savings or current account as inoperative if there are no customer-induced transactions in it for over two years. Such accounts are segregated to reduce the risk of fraud, and they can be reactivated by updating KYC at any branch, free of charge.
steps: No customer-induced transaction for more than 2 years → inoperative
solution.why_others_wrong: Ten years is the period after which the balance goes to the DEA Fund; one and five years are not RBI's inoperative-account period.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Two years

fact_checks.claim: A savings/current account shall be treated as inoperative if there are no customer induced transactions for a period of over two years

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Credit balances in a bank deposit account that has not been operated for how long are transferred to RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund?

solution.explanation: Under the DEA Fund Scheme, 2014, banks transfer to the DEA Fund the credit balance of any deposit account not operated for 10 years or more, and any amount unclaimed for 10 years or more. The depositor can still claim the money from the bank later.
steps: Inoperative/unclaimed for 10 years → transferred to DEA Fund
solution.why_others_wrong: Two years makes an account inoperative but it stays with the bank; 5 and 7 years are not the DEA threshold.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 10 years or more

fact_checks.claim: Amounts credited to DEA Fund are credit balances in deposit accounts not operated for 10 years or more, or unclaimed for 10 years or more

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's April 2025 instructions on deposit accounts of minors, minors above what minimum age limit may be allowed by banks to open and operate savings or term deposit accounts independently?

options.text: An age limit fixed by the bank that is not less than 10 years
An age limit fixed by the bank that is not less than 15 years

solution.explanation: RBI's circular of 21 April 2025 lets banks allow minors above an age limit of not less than 10 years (and up to the amounts and terms the bank fixes under its risk policy) to open and operate savings or term deposit accounts independently. Minors' accounts must never be overdrawn.
steps: That limit cannot be below 10 years
solution.why_others_wrong: 18 years is majority, when no such permission is needed; the floor is 10, not 15; a minor of any age can open an account only through a guardian.
solution.final_answer: Option A: An age limit fixed by the bank that is not less than 10 years

fact_checks.claim: Minors above such an age limit not less than 10 years ... may be allowed to open and operate savings/term deposit accounts independently (circular dated April 21, 2025)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The issued capital of a Regional Rural Bank is subscribed by the Central Government, the State Government and the sponsor bank in which proportion?

solution.explanation: RRBs, set up under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, are jointly owned by the Government of India, the State Government concerned and the sponsor bank, which subscribe the issued capital in the proportion 50%, 15% and 35% respectively.
solution.why_others_wrong: The sponsor bank holds 35%, not 15%; the Centre holds 50%; 51:24:25 is not the RRB pattern.

fact_checks.claim: The issued capital of RRBs is subscribed by Central Government, State Government and sponsor banks in the proportion of 50%, 15% and 35%, respectively
RRBs were established under the provisions of the RRBs Act, 1976

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How often is an individual entitled to one free full credit report, including the credit score, from each credit information company?

solution.explanation: RBI's financial awareness material states that individuals can access one free full credit report (FFCR), including the credit score, once a calendar year from the credit information companies. A higher score usually lets a borrower get loans at a lower rate.
steps: Free full credit report: once every calendar year
solution.why_others_wrong: The free report is annual, not monthly or quarterly, and it is not a one-time facility.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Once a calendar year

fact_checks.claim: Individuals have access to one free full credit report (FFCR) including credit score, once a calendar year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From 1 November 2025, under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, how many nominees can a depositor name for a deposit account?

solution.explanation: Sections 10 to 13 of the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, which deal with nomination, came into force on 1 November 2025. A customer may nominate up to four persons, simultaneously (with shares adding to 100%) or successively, for deposit accounts.
solution.why_others_wrong: Earlier only a single nominee was possible; two and ten are not the limits in the amended law.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Up to four

fact_checks.claim: Provisions on nomination effective 1st November 2025; customers may nominate up to four persons, either simultaneously or successively

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 redefined the threshold for 'substantial interest' in a company, a limit unchanged since 1968, from ₹5 lakh to:

solution.explanation: The provisions brought into force from 1 August 2025 raised the 'substantial interest' threshold from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore. The same stage also raised the maximum tenure of directors (other than the chairperson and whole-time directors) in co-operative banks from 8 to 10 years.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹50 lakh, ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore are not the new threshold.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹2 crore

fact_checks.claim: Redefine the threshold of 'substantial interest' from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore, a limit unchanged since 1968; provisions in force from 1st August 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund was established by RBI under which provision?

options.text: Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949

solution.concept: Legal basis of the DEA Fund
solution.explanation: RBI framed the DEA Fund Scheme, 2014 using its powers under Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the scheme came into effect on 24 May 2014. The fund receives unclaimed deposits of 10 years or more and is used for depositor education and awareness.
solution.why_others_wrong: Section 45ZA is on the inflation target, Section 42 on CRR, and Section 13 of SARFAESI on enforcement of security interest.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949

fact_checks.claim: DEA Fund Scheme, 2014 formulated by RBI under Section 26A of the BR Act, 1949; effective May 24, 2014

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The last customer-induced transaction in Meera's savings account was on 14 March 2016, and the account has remained unoperated and unclaimed since then. Under the DEA Fund Scheme, when must the bank transfer the balance, and what happens to her right to the money?

options.text: On the last working day of April 2026, with accrued interest; she can still claim it from the bank
On 14 March 2026, without interest; her claim lapses after that
On the last working day of March 2026; she can claim it only from RBI
On 14 March 2018, when the account became inoperative; she can claim it only from RBI

solution.explanation: An account not operated for 10 years must be transferred, with accrued interest, on the last working day of the month following the month in which the 10 years are completed. Ten years end on 14 March 2026, so the transfer is due on the last working day of April 2026. The money still belongs to the depositor, who claims it from the bank; the bank then claims a refund from the DEA Fund.
steps: Month subsequent: April 2026 → last working day
Claim lies with the bank, with no time limit
solution.why_others_wrong: Transfer is not on the anniversary date or in the same month; inoperative status after two years does not trigger a transfer; claims are made to the bank, not to RBI, and they do not lapse.
solution.final_answer: Option A: On the last working day of April 2026, with accrued interest; she can still claim it from the bank

fact_checks.claim: Banks transfer the balance to the DEA Fund on the last working day of the month subsequent to the month of completing 10 years of continuous inoperative or unclaimed status
A savings/current account is inoperative after two years without customer induced transactions

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about nomination under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025:
I. For a deposit account, a depositor may choose either simultaneous or successive nomination.
II. For articles in safe custody and safety lockers, simultaneous nomination with fixed percentage shares is permitted.
III. In simultaneous nomination, the shares specified for the nominees must add up to 100 per cent.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Depositors may opt for simultaneous or successive nomination for deposit accounts (I is right). In simultaneous nomination each of up to four nominees gets a specified share, and the shares must total 100% (III is right). For safe custody articles and lockers, only successive nomination is permitted (II is wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including II is wrong, and 'I only' leaves out the correct statement III.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: Deposit accounts: simultaneous or successive nominations; safe custody articles and lockers: only successive nominations; simultaneous shares must total 100 percent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Lead Bank Scheme, which envisaged an 'area approach' to banking to meet credit gaps, was introduced in:

solution.explanation: In December 1969, months after the nationalisation of 14 banks, the Lead Bank Scheme was introduced. It assigned districts to banks under an area approach so that credit gaps could be identified and met.
solution.why_others_wrong: July 1955 is the formation of SBI, April 1980 the second nationalisation and July 1982 the setting up of NABARD.
solution.final_answer: Option D: December 1969

fact_checks.claim: Dec 1969: Lead Bank Scheme introduced which envisaged an area approach to banking to meet the credit gaps

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The first-ever three-way amalgamation in Indian banking, effective 1 April 2019, merged Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank into which bank?

solution.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the amalgamation of Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank (transferor banks) into Bank of Baroda (transferee bank) in January 2019. It took effect on 1 April 2019 and created India's second largest bank at the time.
solution.why_others_wrong: PNB, Canara Bank and Union Bank of India were transferee banks in the 2020 consolidation, not in 2019.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Bank of Baroda

fact_checks.claim: Cabinet approves first-ever three way merger with amalgamation of Vijaya, Dena and Bank of Baroda
The amalgamation comes into effect from 1st April 2019; the amalgamated bank will be named Bank of Baroda

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The 1975 report that shifted bank lending for working capital from a security-based approach to a need-based approach linked to the borrower's production plans was submitted by the:

solution.explanation: The Tandon Committee report (August 1975) emphasised correlating bank credit with borrowers' business or production plans and own resources. Its norms formed the basis of bank lending for working capital.
steps: 1975 + working capital + need-based lending → Tandon Committee
solution.why_others_wrong: The Chore Committee (1980) dealt with the cash credit system; Narasimham (1991) with financial sector reforms; Nayak (2014) with governance of bank boards.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Tandon Committee

fact_checks.claim: 09 Aug 1975: Tandon Committee Report emphasized need to correlate bank credit to the business/ production plans; shift from security based to need based approach

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Along with five associate banks, which bank was merged with the State Bank of India with effect from 1 April 2017?

solution.explanation: Under Government orders of February and March 2017, State Bank of Bikaner and Jaipur, State Bank of Hyderabad, State Bank of Mysore, State Bank of Patiala and State Bank of Travancore, and the Bharatiya Mahila Bank, merged with SBI with effect from 1 April 2017.
steps: Five associates + Bharatiya Mahila Bank → SBI, 1 April 2017
solution.why_others_wrong: Dena Bank merged into Bank of Baroda (2019); Oriental Bank of Commerce into PNB (2020); IDBI Bank was not merged with SBI.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Bharatiya Mahila Bank

fact_checks.claim: Erstwhile associate banks (SBBJ, SBH, SBM, SBP, SBT) merged with SBI as per Government order dated February 22, 2017
All branches of Bharatiya Mahila Bank Limited will function as branches of SBI from April 1, 2017

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Banks Board Bureau, which started functioning in April 2016, was set up on the recommendation of the committee chaired by:

solution.explanation: RBI's Committee to Review Governance of Boards of Banks in India (chairman P. J. Nayak, report May 2014) recommended a Bank Boards Bureau to advise on board appointments, as a step towards a Bank Investment Company. The Banks Board Bureau began functioning on 8 April 2016.
steps: Governance of bank boards → P. J. Nayak Committee (2014)
solution.why_others_wrong: Narasimham chaired the banking sector reform committees; Urjit Patel the monetary policy framework committee; Chore the cash credit review.
solution.final_answer: Option D: P. J. Nayak

fact_checks.claim: Committee to Review Governance of Boards of Banks in India report dated 13 May 2014
Following the Nayak Committee recommendations, the BBB was set up and started functioning from April 8, 2016

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
I. Formation of DICGC by merging the Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India
II. Introduction of the Lead Bank Scheme
III. Establishment of NABARD
IV. Submission of the Tandon Committee report

solution.explanation: Lead Bank Scheme: December 1969. Tandon Committee report: August 1975. DICGC formed with effect from 15 July 1978. NABARD established on 12 July 1982.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other option misplaces either the Tandon report (1975) or NABARD (1982), which is the latest event.
solution.final_answer: Option B: II, IV, I, III

fact_checks.claim: Lead Bank Scheme Dec 1969; Tandon Committee Report 9 Aug 1975; DICGC formed wef July 15, 1978; NABARD established 12 July 1982

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Match the committee or body with its subject:
1. Tandon Committee (1975)
2. Chore Committee (1980)
3. Banking Commission (1969)
4. P. J. Nayak Committee (2014)
P. Governance of boards of banks
Q. Working capital finance on a need-based approach
R. Review of the cash credit system
S. Banking costs, banking legislation and indigenous banking

solution.explanation: Tandon (1975) tied working capital lending to production plans; Chore (recommendations adopted in December 1980) reviewed the cash credit system; the Banking Commission (set up January 1969) was to report on banking costs, legislation, indigenous banking and procedures; Nayak (2014) reviewed governance of bank boards.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping Tandon and Chore, or the Banking Commission and Nayak, gives the wrong subjects.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 1-Q, 2-R, 3-S, 4-P

fact_checks.claim: Tandon Committee 1975 on need-based working capital; Chore Committee recommendations on the cash credit system adopted Dec 1980; Banking Commission set up 29 Jan 1969 to report on banking costs, legislation, indigenous banking
P. J. Nayak committee reviewed governance of boards of banks in India (2014)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
I. The amalgamation of Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank with Bank of Baroda was the first three-way consolidation of banks in India.
II. The associate banks of SBI that merged with it in 2017 included State Bank of Travancore and State Bank of Patiala.
III. Vijaya Bank was merged into Canara Bank in 2020.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The BoB–Vijaya–Dena amalgamation (1 April 2019) was the first three-way consolidation (I right). SBBJ, SBH, SBM, SBP and SBT merged with SBI from 1 April 2017 (II right). Vijaya Bank became part of Bank of Baroda in 2019, not Canara Bank (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement III is false, so options containing it are wrong; 'I only' omits the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: First-ever three-way merger of Vijaya, Dena and Bank of Baroda
State Bank of Bikaner and Jaipur, Hyderabad, Mysore, Patiala and Travancore merged with SBI w.e.f. April 1, 2017

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For what period are directors appointed or nominated to RBI's Central Board?

solution.explanation: RBI's affairs are governed by a Central Board appointed by the Government of India under the RBI Act. Directors are appointed or nominated for a period of four years.
solution.why_others_wrong: Two, three and five years are not the term stated by RBI.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Four years

fact_checks.claim: Central Board appointed by the Government of India; appointed/nominated for a period of four years

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to the Preamble of the RBI Act as RBI describes it, the monetary policy framework aims to:

options.text: Maximise employment while keeping inflation below 2%
Maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth
Maintain a fixed exchange rate of the rupee
Finance the fiscal deficit of the Government

solution.explanation: RBI's Preamble describes its functions as regulating the issue of bank notes and keeping reserves for monetary stability, operating the currency and credit system, and having a modern monetary policy framework 'to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth'.
steps: Objective: price stability, keeping growth in mind
solution.why_others_wrong: A maximum-employment mandate belongs to other central banks; India has no fixed exchange-rate target; automatic financing of the deficit ended with ad hoc T-bills.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth

fact_checks.claim: Preamble: to have a modern monetary policy framework ... to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following persons is NOT among RBI's Deputy Governors listed on RBI's Central Board in November 2026?

solution.explanation: RBI's Central Board page lists Governor Sanjay Malhotra and four Deputy Governors: Swaminathan J, Dr. Poonam Gupta, Shirish Chandra Murmu and Rohit Jain. Michael Debabrata Patra is a former Deputy Governor and is not on the current list.
steps: Current DGs: Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, S. C. Murmu, Rohit Jain
M. D. Patra is not listed
solution.why_others_wrong: Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta and Rohit Jain are all listed as Deputy Governors.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Michael Debabrata Patra

fact_checks.claim: Central Board: Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor; Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J, Dr. Poonam Gupta, Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu, Shri Rohit Jain

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following institutions is fully funded by the Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Indian Institute of Banking and Finance (IIBF)
Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)

solution.explanation: RBI lists CAFRAL and IGIDR as fully funded by it. For IIBM, RBI is a sponsor along with other banks; for NIBM it is an ordinary member. IDRBT is an autonomous training establishment, not a part of RBI.
steps: IIBM: sponsor; NIBM: member; IDRBT: autonomous
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI is only an ordinary member of NIBM and one of the sponsors of IIBM; IIBF is not among the institutes RBI lists as fully funded by it.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Manmohan Singh, who later became Prime Minister, was appointed Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in:

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records Manmohan Singh's appointment as Governor on 16 September 1982. He was followed by A. Ghosh (briefly) and R. N. Malhotra in 1985.
solution.why_others_wrong: May 1977 is M. Narasimham's appointment, February 1985 R. N. Malhotra's and June 1970 S. Jagannathan's.
solution.final_answer: Option A: September 1982

fact_checks.claim: 16 Sep 1982: Manmohan Singh appointed Governor; 04 Feb 1985: RN Malhotra appointed Governor; 02 May 1977: M. Narasimham; 16 Jun 1970: S. Jagannathan

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Board for Financial Supervision (BFS), which exercises integrated supervision over banks, financial institutions and NBFCs, was constituted in:

solution.explanation: The BFS was constituted in November 1994 as a committee of RBI's Central Board under the RBI (Board for Financial Supervision) Regulations, 1994. The Department of Supervision provides it secretarial support.
steps: BFS: November 1994, committee of the Central Board
solution.why_others_wrong: 1935 is RBI's establishment, January 1949 its nationalisation, and 2016 relates to the MPC framework.
solution.final_answer: Option C: November 1994

fact_checks.claim: BFS constituted in November 1994 as a committee of the Central Board under the RBI (BFS) Regulations, 1994; integrated supervision over commercial banks, FIs and NBFCs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following Acts is NOT among those administered by the Reserve Bank of India, as listed by RBI?

solution.explanation: RBI lists the Acts it administers: the RBI Act, Public Debt Act/Government Securities Act, BR Act, FEMA, SARFAESI (Chapter II), CIC (Regulation) Act 2005, PSS Act 2007 and Factoring Regulation Act 2011. The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 appears only among 'other relevant Acts'.
steps: Administered: CIC Act, PSS Act, Factoring Act, etc.
solution.why_others_wrong: The CIC Act, Factoring Regulation Act and PSS Act are all in RBI's list of Acts it administers.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

fact_checks.claim: Acts administered by RBI include the CIC (Regulation) Act 2005, PSS Act 2007 and Factoring Regulation Act 2011; the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 is listed under other relevant Acts

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Arrange the following RBI Governors in the order of their appointment:
I. S. Jagannathan
II. R. N. Malhotra
III. I. G. Patel
IV. M. Narasimham

solution.explanation: S. Jagannathan was appointed on 16 June 1970, M. Narasimham on 2 May 1977, I. G. Patel on 1 December 1977, and R. N. Malhotra on 4 February 1985.
solution.why_others_wrong: Narasimham's short tenure (May–November 1977) came just before I. G. Patel's; Malhotra came last.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I, IV, III, II

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Rupee coins of one rupee and above are legal tender for any sum not exceeding how much in a single transaction?

solution.explanation: Under the Coinage Act, 2011, a coin of one rupee or more is legal tender for any sum not exceeding ₹1,000 in a single transaction, and the 50 paise coin for any sum not exceeding ₹10. Accepting more voluntarily is not prohibited.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹10 is the limit for 50 paise coins; ₹100 and ₹10,000 are not legal-tender limits.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹1,000

fact_checks.claim: Coin of any denomination not lower than one rupee shall be legal tender for any sum not exceeding one thousand rupee in any single transaction; fifty paise coin not exceeding ten rupee

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The two banknote presses owned by RBI through its wholly owned subsidiary Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Pvt. Ltd. (BRBNMPL) are located at:

solution.explanation: Banknotes are printed at four presses: SPMCIL (Government-owned) runs those at Nashik and Dewas, and BRBNMPL (RBI-owned) runs those at Mysuru and Salboni. Coins are minted at SPMCIL's mints at Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and NOIDA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Nashik and Dewas are SPMCIL presses; Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and NOIDA are mints for coins.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Mysuru and Salboni

fact_checks.claim: Two presses of BRBNMPL are at Mysuru and Salboni; SPMCIL presses at Nasik and Dewas; mints at Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and NOIDA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under Section 24 of the RBI Act, 1934, bank notes can be issued in such other denominational values as the Central Government may specify on the Central Board's recommendation, but not exceeding:

solution.explanation: Section 24 lists denominations from ₹2 to ₹10,000 and allows other values the Central Government may specify on the Central Board's recommendation, 'not exceeding ten thousand rupees'. The highest note ever printed was the ₹10,000 note, last demonetised in 1978.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹2,000 is the highest note currently issued; ₹5,000 was an old denomination; ₹1 lakh is beyond the ceiling.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹10,000

fact_checks.claim: Section 24: bank notes of such other denominational values, not exceeding ten thousand rupees, as the Central Government may specify

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In January 1978, RBI's records show that banknotes of which denominations were demonetised?

solution.explanation: High-denomination notes of ₹1,000, ₹5,000 and ₹10,000, reintroduced in 1954, were demonetised on 16 January 1978 to curb illicit transfer of money. The ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes of the Mahatma Gandhi series were withdrawn in November 2016.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹500/₹1,000 is the 2016 demonetisation; ₹2,000 notes were withdrawn from circulation in 2023 but remain legal tender.

fact_checks.claim: Notes of Rs 1,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000 denominations demonetised on 16 Jan 1978
₹1000, ₹5000 and ₹10000 banknotes reintroduced in 1954 were again demonetized in January 1978

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following describes RBI's role as banker to the Government, as stated by RBI?

options.text: It acts as banker only to the Central Government; States must bank with SBI
It performs merchant banking functions for the Central and State governments and also acts as their banker
It lends to the Government without limit to finance the fiscal deficit
It acts as banker to the Government only for foreign exchange transactions

solution.explanation: RBI describes its related function as banker to the Government: it performs merchant banking functions for the Central and State governments and also acts as their banker. As banker to banks, it maintains the banking accounts of all scheduled banks.
steps: Banker to Central and State governments + merchant banking function
solution.why_others_wrong: States also bank with RBI; automatic unlimited financing of deficits does not exist; the role is not limited to foreign exchange.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It performs merchant banking functions for the Central and State governments and also acts as their banker

fact_checks.claim: Banker to the Government: performs merchant banking function for the central and the state governments; also acts as their banker. Banker to banks: maintains banking accounts of all scheduled banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about bank notes:
I. 'Star series' notes replace defectively printed notes in a packet of 100 serially numbered notes.
II. Two banknotes can carry the same serial number if they differ in inset letter, year of printing or the Governor's signature.
III. Non-sequential numbering of notes in packets was introduced in 2011.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI adopted the Star series to replace defectively printed notes in a packet of 100 serially numbered notes (I). Notes with the same serial number are possible if the inset letter, year of printing or Governor's signature differs (II). Non-sequential numbering was introduced in 2011 for efficiency (III). All three are correct.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other options leaves out at least one correct statement.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I, II and III

fact_checks.claim: Star series used for replacement of defectively printed banknotes in a packet of 100; same serial number possible with different inset letter, year or signature; non-sequential numbering introduced in 2011

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A shopkeeper is offered three payments in separate transactions: (P) ₹800 in ₹10 coins, (Q) ₹1,500 in ₹5 coins, (R) ₹20 in 50 paise coins. Under the Coinage Act, 2011, which of these can the shopkeeper NOT be compelled to accept?

solution.explanation: Rupee coins (₹1 and above) are legal tender up to ₹1,000 in a single transaction, so P (₹800) must be accepted but Q (₹1,500) can be refused. 50 paise coins are legal tender only up to ₹10, so R (₹20) can be refused. Voluntary acceptance beyond these limits is not prohibited.

fact_checks.claim: All digital payment transactions shall be authenticated by at least two distinct factors; for transactions other than card present, at least one factor is dynamically created or proven; compliance by April 01, 2026

questions.question_text: Under RBI's 2025 directions on lending against gold and silver, what is the cap on the aggregate weight of coins a borrower may pledge for all loans?

options.text: 50 grams of gold coins and 500 grams of silver coins
1 kg of gold coins and 10 kg of silver coins
100 grams of gold coins and 1 kg of silver coins

solution.explanation: Coins pledged by a borrower for all loans may not exceed 50 grams of gold coins and 500 grams of silver coins. For ornaments, the caps are 1 kg of gold and 10 kg of silver.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 kg/10 kg are the ornament limits; 100 g/1 kg are not prescribed; coins are capped.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 50 grams of gold coins and 500 grams of silver coins

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Authentication Mechanisms Directions, 2025, who bears the loss if a digital payment is put through without complying with the Directions?

options.text: The customer bears the loss up to ₹10,000
The loss is shared equally by issuer and customer
The payment system operator bears it only if the customer reports within 30 days
The issuer must compensate the customer for the loss in full, without demur

solution.explanation: The Directions state that if any loss arises from transactions effected without complying with them, the issuer shall compensate the customer for the loss in full without demur.
steps: Non-compliant transaction → issuer compensates in full
solution.why_others_wrong: The Directions place full liability on the issuer, with no sharing or customer threshold.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The issuer must compensate the customer for the loss in full, without demur

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A borrower pledges gold jewellery valued at ₹3.5 lakh for a consumption loan. Under the LTV tiers of RBI's 2025 gold and silver lending directions, what is the maximum loan he can get?

solution.explanation: LTV depends on the loan amount: 85% up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% above ₹2.5 lakh up to ₹5 lakh. 85% of ₹3.5 lakh = ₹2.975 lakh, but that exceeds ₹2.5 lakh, so the 80% tier applies: 80% × 3.5 = ₹2.80 lakh, which lies within the ₹2.5–5 lakh band. So the maximum is ₹2.80 lakh.
steps: 85% × 3.5 = 2.975 > 2.5 → 85% tier not available for this amount
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹2.975 lakh wrongly applies 85% to a loan above ₹2.5 lakh; ₹2.50 lakh stops at the first tier; ₹2.625 lakh applies 75%.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹2.80 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Maximum LTV for consumption loans: 85 per cent up to ₹2.5 lakh; 80 per cent above ₹2.5 lakh and up to ₹5 lakh

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's 2025 directions on lending against gold and silver:
I. Loans cannot be given against primary gold or silver, or against units of gold ETFs or gold mutual funds.
II. Loans cannot be given for the purchase of gold in any form.
III. Detailed assessment of repayment capacity is required for every gold loan, whatever its size.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The directions bar lending against primary gold/silver and against financial assets backed by them, such as ETF or MF units (I right), and bar lending to purchase gold in any form (II right). Detailed credit assessment is mandatory only where total loans against eligible collateral exceed ₹2.5 lakh per borrower (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: III ignores the ₹2.5 lakh threshold, so options including it are wrong; 'I only' omits II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: No lending against primary gold or silver or financial assets backed by them such as ETF or MF units; no lending for purchase of gold in any form; detailed credit assessment where the total loan amount against eligible collateral is above ₹2.5 lakh
